verdicts.reason: A shrinks the shoe to a tiny icon jammed into the left edge and spreads the small logo, headline and CTA across a mostly empty banner, so it has no focal point. B gives the shoe real presence on the left, but the logo is off-axis from the headline column, the 'Run lighter' headline is still undersized for the banner, and the CTA floats far from its copy.

A is the same weak layout: tiny shoe, scattered centred text, a weak headline and large dead areas. B groups the text and CTA as a left column and puts a large shoe on the right, which reads properly left to right. Its left edges are ragged, though: the logo, headline/subcopy and button all start at different x positions, and the shoe sits low and close to the right and bottom edges.

A has the tiny shoe pinned to the left edge, and its centred text has no hierarchy or weight. B reads well left to right (copy, then the large shoe, then the CTA), but the logo isn't aligned with the headline/subcopy column, the subcopy sits low and close to the bottom edge, and the headline is still small relative to the shoe.
